definitions.explanation: The act of getting involved in a situation, dispute, or matter, often when one is not directly a party to it. Used for both positive interventions (helping) and negative ones (meddling).

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}が{市場|しじょう}に{介入|かいにゅう}した。
examples.english: The government intervened in the market.

examples.japanese: {他国|たこく}の{内政|ないせい}に{介入|かいにゅう}すべきではない。
examples.english: We shouldn't intervene in other countries' internal affairs.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}が{介入|かいにゅう}して{事態|じたい}を{収|おさ}めた。
examples.english: The police stepped in and resolved the situation.

notes:
KANJI BREAKDOWN:
・{介|かい} - mediate, between
・{入|にゅう} - to enter

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{市場|しじょう}{介入|かいにゅう} - market intervention
・{為替|かわせ}{介入|かいにゅう} - currency intervention
・{軍事|ぐんじ}{介入|かいにゅう} - military intervention
・{内政|ないせい}{介入|かいにゅう} - interference in domestic affairs
・{介入|かいにゅう}を{避|さ}ける - to avoid intervening

CONTEXT:
{介入|かいにゅう} is common in:
・{政治|せいじ} - politics (government/international intervention)
・{経済|けいざい} - economics (market/currency intervention)
・{紛争|ふんそう} - conflict resolution
・{人間関係|にんげんかんけい} - interpersonal matters

NUANCE:
Can be positive (helping to resolve a situation) or negative (meddling in others' affairs), depending on context.

RELATED VOCABULARY:
・{干渉|かんしょう} - interference (more negative nuance)
・{関与|かんよ} - involvement, participation
・{仲裁|ちゅうさい} - mediation, arbitration

REGISTER:
Neutral to formal. Common in news, politics, and formal discussions.
